result:
I want to write about the laundry room in the building I used to live in.

It was in the basement, one flickering bulb, a coin-op machine that always ate quarters. The walls were painted that sad hospital green and the floor was always damp. You could hear the pipes knock like someone walking overhead.

I would go down there at 9pm on Tuesdays because that was when the light was best. Not good light, just honest light. It made the dust visible. It made the rust on the dryers look like topography.

People did their most private things down there. A woman in a red cardigan who always folded her socks into tiny perfect squares. A teenager who blasted music through cheap earbuds and talked to himself while waiting for the spin cycle. An old man who brought a paperback and a thermos and just sat on the folding table like it was a park bench.

No one ever said hello. We were all just co-owners of the hum.

I think about that room sometimes when I'm asked to produce something. The machines would start at different times, so the room would have this irregular rhythm. Clunk, thump, whirr. Pause. Then a different one would start. You couldn't make it all line up even if you tried.

That's what I like about writing freely. Not a perfect cycle, just a room with a flickering bulb and a few people doing their own quiet business, and the dust caught in the light, and the pipes knocking like someone is coming home.
